name: Roberto Rocca
notes: Roberto Rocca, longtime head of Argentina's Techint group and first chairman of Tenaris, died in Milan on 10 June 2003 aged 81 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Rocca). The group is now led by his son Paolo Rocca.

name: Carl Ray Pohlad
notes: Carl Pohlad, Minnesota financier and Minnesota Twins owner from 1984, died 5 January 2009 aged 93 (source: https://www.mprnews.org/story/2009/01/05/pohlad1). The family business continues as Pohlad Companies.

name: Andreas E.Rihs
notes: Andy Rihs, co-founder and longtime CEO/chairman of Phonak/Sonova and backer of the BMC cycling team, died 18 April 2018 aged 75 (source: https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/cycling-supporter_swiss-entrepreneur-and-bmc-cycling-backer-andy-rihs-has-died/44058924).

name: Ryuji Arai
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder, Bic Camera Inc. (Tokyo)
profile: Ryuji Arai founded Bic Camera, the Japanese electronics and appliance retail chain. It began in 1968 as a photo-processing business in Takasaki, Gunma, became Bic Color, and was renamed Bic Camera in 1978, with its first store in Ikebukuro. It listed in 2006 and posted over $6B in revenue in FY Aug 2025. Arai also holds stakes in Hit Communications and contact-lens maker Seed.
interesting_fact: Bic Camera owns a majority stake in the listed satellite TV network Nippon BS Broadcasting (BS11).
deep_cut_fact: Arai's first venture, started in his early twenties, was Takasaki DP Center, a film developing and printing shop in Gunma. Bic Camera grew out of that shop's camera-sales department, which was spun off as Bic Color in 1972.
notes: Very reclusive and gives essentially no interviews (Bic Camera declined to make him available to Bloomberg in 2018). Best route is Bic Camera's PR/IR department via its IR site. A 2009 government press file listed the address kouhou@biccamera.com for PR/IR, but it is old and unverified, so it is not included. He is known as an anti-nuclear advocate: Bic Camera hung banners in 1995 protesting French nuclear tests (https://macaudailytimes.com.mo/?p=91929).
